newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Matos to continue debt talks in N.Y.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Matos to continue debt talks in N.Y.

text.p: Venezuelan officials will meet in New York next week with bankers to pin down restructuring plans for payments on its $35 billion of international debt, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar said.
"We'll be meeting with various banks to firm up plans when I fly to New York next week," Matos told reporters.
Some 15 banks have already presented proposals that "reduce the budget's debt burden, so liberating resources for special spending or investment," Matos added. He did not provide details.

Debt service payments account for some 35 percent of the government budget. Among its debts, Venezuela has around $18 billion of restructured Brady debt, another $7 billion of non- restructured commercial debt, while state-owned oil company PdVSA holds another $4 billion.
